Definition: Whether the system enables individuals to authenticate themselves or their documents digitally through electronic verification
Comments: The new AES biometric e-ID card is designed to 'enable secure online identification' and support digital authentication. The nigeridentite.com portal lists banking authentication and digital payments as e-ID functions. The June 2025 MoU describes online authentication for e-government and e-banking as target functionalities of the new e-ID system.

Definition: Whether authentication is possible through a centralized government portal or digital gateway
Comments: The nigeridentite.com portal lists 'access to public administration services (Services Administratifs)' as a primary e-ID function. The June 2025 MoU and associated press describe e-government as a core use case: 'E-gouvernement, E-finance, E-Banking' services enabled by the new e-ID. Government portal authentication is a designed capability of the new system.

Definition: Whether individuals can view their data held in the ID database and see how it has been accessed
Comments: Niger's Law No. 2022-59 (Data Protection Act, Article 69) grants data subjects the right to access: confirmation of whether personal data is processed, a copy of their personal data, information on data origins, purposes of processing, and recipients. This right of individual access to personal data held in identity systems is enshrined in law.

Definition: Whether the system enables Know Your Customer (KYC) packet collection for service provision, particularly financial services
Comments: The AES biometric ID card features a multifunctional chip enabling 'secure verification for government services, banking, and border crossings' (Business Insider Africa, December 2025). The June 2025 MoU explicitly targets E-Banking and financial service access. The e-ID card enables KYC for financial institutions per design specifications.

Definition: Whether the ID authority and system are subject to general oversight of the courts and judicial review
Value Name: Yes, but not specific to ID
Comments: Decisions of the HAPDP (data protection authority) are subject to appeal before the Conseil d'État (Council of State) per the 2022 Personal Data Protection Act. This provides judicial oversight over data protection decisions affecting digital ID. No dedicated ID-specific judicial oversight mechanism has been identified in available sources.

Definition: Whether the civil registration and digital ID systems are integrated
Comments: APAI-CRVS assessment found Niger has CRVS electronic databases in urban towns only. The WURI World Bank project includes linkage between foundational ID credentials and civil registration. The HAPDP received a Ministerial request to review the unique identification process (connected to WURI's CRVS integration efforts, 2024). However, approximately 83% of Nigeriens live in rural areas with many births unregistered, indicating partial integration.

Definition: Whether procedural rules for collection, storage, and sharing of ID-related personal data are publicly available and established
Comments: Law No. 2022-59 of 16 December 2022 (Data Protection Act) establishes data sharing rules requiring prior consent, purpose limitation, and notification of data subjects about third-party data sharing. Cross-border transfers require equivalent protection. Processing requires prior notification to HAPDP. Rules are codified in law but specific operational data sharing frameworks for the ID system are not fully published.

Definition: Whether specific regulation or policy addresses digital ID beyond general identification legislation
Comments: Niger's Council of Ministers adopted a specific decree on 26 December 2025 establishing the AES biometric national identity card (Carte Nationale d'Identité Biométrique AES) and AES electronic passport. This constitutes digital ID-specific regulation. The HAPDP article also references Ministerial solicitation for data protection review in context of the unique identification process.

Definition: Whether national data protection legislation exists and covers personal data linked to the ID system
Comments: Niger has a comprehensive data protection law: Law No. 2017-28 of 3 May 2017 on Protection of Personal Data, subsequently amended by Law No. 2019-71 of 24 December 2019, Law No. 2022-59 of 16 December 2022 (new consolidated act), and Law No. 2023-31 of 4 July 2023. The law governs collection, processing, storage and transfer of personal data including biometric data.

Definition: Whether a Data Protection Authority or similar body regulates ID data collection and sharing by the ID system
Comments: The Haute Autorité de Protection des Données à caractère Personnel (HAPDP) was established by Law No. 2017-28 of 3 May 2017 and became operational in 2020. It is an independent administrative authority attached to the Presidency of the Republic, responsible for ensuring compliance with data protection law. The Ministry of Interior consulted the HAPDP regarding the WURI unique identification process (2024). The HAPDP has a strategic plan 2021-2025.

Definition: Whether the digital ID credential serves as legal proof of an individual's identity as codified in law
Comments: Niger's national identity card (Carte Nationale d'Identité) is accepted as legal proof of identity under Niger's Electoral Code (Code électoral), which lists the CIN as primary acceptable identification document. The December 2025 decree mandating the AES biometric ID card for all citizens aged 15+ and requiring it for access to public services, travel, banking, and official transactions confirms its legal proof status.

Definition: Whether formal legislation (act, law, regulation) governs digital identity including identification acts, digital ID laws, or equivalent legislation
Comments: Niger has a legal framework for national identity. A pre-existing ordonnance establishes the Carte Nationale d'Identité (obligatory from age 15). The December 2025 decree by the Council of Ministers formally establishes the AES biometric national identity card system. The WURI Phase 2 project (World Bank) includes a component to strengthen the legal and institutional framework for digital ID in Niger.

Definition: Whether the system and the production of credentials can be managed, maintained and developed by in-country technical staff (as opposed to foreign vendors)
Comments: The June 2025 MoU signed between Niger's Ministry of Interior and Libyan firm Al Itissan Al-Jadeed covers the financing, construction, and maintenance of both the biometric e-passport system and the national e-ID card system. The partnership is a public-private arrangement with a foreign vendor responsible for system maintenance.

Definition: Whether the ongoing management, maintenance and development of the ID system can be funded by sustainable domestic resources
Comments: Niger's digital ID development is primarily funded by external sources: the WURI Phase 2 World Bank program (total envelope US$395.1m across participating countries) and the June 2025 MoU with Libyan firm Al Itissan Al-Jadeed which covers financing, construction, and maintenance. The nigeridentite.com portal shows fees (5,000 FCFA for card + 1,000 FCFA dossier) but primary infrastructure investment is externally financed.

Definition: Whether the system collects biometric data and which modalities are collected (fingerprints, facial image, iris scans)
Comments: The new AES biometric national identity card (decree approved December 2025) features a multifunctional electronic chip storing biometric data. The WURI World Bank project supported biometric data collection including fingerprints. The nigeridentite.com portal specifies biometric capture at accredited centers. Sources confirm fingerprint and facial biometric collection; no confirmed iris scanning mentioned in available evidence.

Definition: Whether identity records are stored in electronic/digital format versus paper-based records
Comments: The WURI World Bank project (Phase 2, Niger) established a digital foundational identity platform. The new AES biometric ID system (decree December 2025) includes digital records archiving. The nigeridentite.com portal offers digital enrollment and tracking. APAI-CRVS assessment noted Niger has CRVS electronic databases in urban towns; the national ID database under WURI/e-ID is fully digital.

Definition: Whether the country has established or is actively developing a national digital identity system, including foundational ID systems that enable authentication across multiple services. Fully deployed means operational nationwide and accepting new registrations.
Comments: Niger has a long-standing national identity card (Carte Nationale d'Identité) and the WURI World Bank project (Phase 2, 2020) supports development of a foundational digital ID system. In June 2025 Niger signed MoUs with Libyan firm Al Itissan Al-Jadeed for a new biometric e-ID and e-passport system. On 26 December 2025, the Council of Ministers approved decrees establishing AES biometric national identity cards (mandatory for citizens aged 15+). The nigeridentite.com portal offers online E-ID enrollment. System is actively under development with full deployment not yet completed.

Definition: Whether the digital ID system is designed to be interoperable across government agencies and with other systems through APIs or data exchange protocols
Comments: The new AES biometric e-ID card is explicitly designed to be 'interoperable and compliant with international standards' (June 2025 MoU). The WURI program supported interoperability of foundational ID systems across West Africa. The December 2025 AES biometric ID decree aims to harmonize identity documents across Niger, Mali, and Burkina Faso for cross-border use. However Niger's exit from ECOWAS limits broader regional interoperability.

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for opening bank accounts and accessing financial services
Comments: The December 2025 decree on the AES biometric national identity card states it 'will be required for access to public services, travel, banking, and official transactions' in Niger. The new biometric ID card, with its multifunctional chip, is mandatory for banking access. The June 2025 MoU and associated sources confirm E-Banking as a core use case.

Definition: Whether the digital ID is recognized or interoperable across borders through regional agreements or travel documents
Comments: The December 2025 AES biometric national identity card decree is part of an initiative to harmonize identity documents within the Alliance of Sahel States (AES: Niger, Mali, Burkina Faso). Per Fragomen, 'These AES biometric national identity cards will allow individuals to travel throughout the AES without a passport.' This constitutes formal cross-border interoperability within the AES confederation.

Definition: Age in years at which an individual becomes eligible to register for digital ID
Comments: Niger's national identity card has traditionally been obligatory for citizens aged 15 and above (per existing ordonnance on CIN). The December 2025 decree establishing the AES biometric national identity card explicitly mandates it for 'all citizens aged 15 and above'. Enrollment eligibility threshold is 15 years, falling within the 10-17 age range.

Definition: Whether registration for digital ID is mandatory, optional, or mandatory for specific groups
Comments: The December 2025 Council of Ministers decree establishing the AES biometric national identity card makes it 'compulsory for all citizens aged 15 and above'. The traditional CIN was also described as obligatory (from age 15 when traveling outside one's arrondissement). The new decree signals universal mandatory enrollment.

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for accessing public healthcare services
Comments: The nigeridentite.com portal lists 'digital medical records and healthcare services access' as a core e-ID function. The WURI program includes health programs as a key service access domain for ID credentials. The June 2025 MoU mentions healthcare as a target service. No specific evidence confirms healthcare access is yet mandatory via the digital ID in Niger.

Chapter Details: The architecture, governance, functionality and uptake of government digital identity systems and credentials. 30 variables in 5 sections. Contains latest available data. Data collection by Perplexity from a variety of sources.
Definition: Percentage of eligible population that has been issued or registered with digital ID credentials
Comments: Niger's digital ID system is in early deployment. The WURI case study (2022) noted 55% of the population faces challenges accessing ID due to lack of credentials. Sofrecom (2024) reports ~83% of Nigeriens are rural with many births undeclared. The new AES biometric ID card decree (December 2025) has not yet been implemented nationwide. Digital ID coverage is estimated below 20% of total population.

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for registering for social assistance programs and accessing social services
Comments: The AES biometric ID card decree (December 2025) states the card will be required for 'access to public services' including social protection programs. The June 2025 MoU describes social protection as a key use case ('programmes de protection sociale'). The WURI program explicitly targets social safety nets and social registries as service access domains requiring ID credentials.
